title: Protocol definition
description: Meta-schema for schema/protocol.json: what holds across every message, and the transport underneath them.

endian.description: Byte order every message field uses unless it says otherwise. Absent where nothing has established one for the range.

cipher.description: Applied to a channel payload above the transport, so the transport never sees plaintext.

blockSize.description: In bytes. A payload with no complete block travels unchanged, since there is nothing to encipher.

blockEndian.description: How the bytes of a block map onto the words the algorithm works on. This is a property of the cipher rather than of any field.

keySize.description: Key length in bytes. Both ends hold the key before a connection opens, so nothing on the wire carries it.

padded.description: The directions whose sender pads each payload to a whole number of blocks and enciphers all of it. The bytes it adds follow the message's own fields and hold nothing in particular. Where this is absent, no direction pads.

keyForm.description: How a client takes the key from its launch argument: base64, decoded, or text, its first keySize characters taken as they stand. Where this is absent, base64.

transport.description: The protocol carrying channel payloads, and how it differs from stock.

header.description: The packet header, which differs from the stock one. Fields use the same vocabulary as a message.

constants.description: Values that differ from the stock protocol. Each names what it replaces.

stock.description: What the stock protocol uses, so the difference is visible.
